concepts.title: Cultural Currents between India, Persia, Central and East Asia

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cultural Currents between India, Persia, Central and East Asia' refers to.
questions.a: Between the thirteenth and seventeenth centuries a web of trade, pilgrimage and conquest carried people, books and ideas across Persia, Central Asia, East Asia and India, so art, language and belief flowed along the routes that merchants and travellers opened.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cultural Currents between India, Persia, Central and East Asia'.
questions.a: Trade routes were culture routes: goods travelled with ideas, art and faith.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sufi and Bhakti Currents' refers to.
questions.a: Two devotional movements swept this age: Sufi saints of the Islamic tradition, like the Indo-Persian Sufi poet Amir Khusrau who blended Indian and Persian song, and the Bhakti saints who preached loving devotion in local tongues, both carrying religion to the common people.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sufi and Bhakti Currents'.
questions.a: Sufi and Bhakti saints took faith out of the clergy's hands and into people's languages.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sufi and Bhakti Currents' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Variations in Role and Status: Women and Social Groups

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Variations in Role and Status: Women and Social Groups' refers to.
questions.a: Status in medieval society varied by region, caste and gender: women's roles ranged from royal regents and poet-saints to weavers working in household workshops, and social groups rose or fell as new professions and sects opened different paths.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Variations in Role and Status: Women and Social Groups'.
questions.a: Medieval society was layered and mobile - gender, caste and occupation shaped each life differently.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Variations in Role and Status: Women and Social Groups' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 8 (source: hees209.txt lines 520-540 (variations in their role and status))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Education and Knowledge Traditions' refers to.
questions.a: Learning flourished in maktabs, madrasas, pathshalas and temple schools: mathematics, astronomy, medicine, music and craft knowledge were taught and exchanged, with manuscripts moving across Asia to keep India part of the medieval world of learning.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Education and Knowledge Traditions'.
questions.a: Schools of many faiths and craft guilds of many skills kept knowledge alive and travelling.
